queries.not_checked: fol: compares the line endings of two systems (the same as Windows)
fol: compares the line endings of two systems (different from Windows)

fol.notes: Systems are an uninterpreted sort; uses_line_ending is read as a function to an enumeration of line endings (one per system: the questions ask 'which line ending' and 'the same line ending', the DL file's firm one_ending), so different endings are distinct. As the DL file: Linux is Unix-like in every world; w1 has its line ending stored by name, w2 reaches it only through the deleted rule. Windows' CRLF is a stored bridge (q3) and given in q1's prompt.

linux_member.says: Linux is a Unix-like operating system. (stored)

windows_crlf.says: Microsoft Windows uses a carriage return followed by a line feed (CRLF) to end lines in text files. (stored)

halyard_member.says: Halyard OS is a Unix-like operating system.

windows_crlf.says: Microsoft Windows uses CRLF line endings.

label_corrections.why: 'The same line ending as Windows' is a join through a functional line-ending link to named individuals: halyard : uses_line_ending some (inv(uses_line_ending) value windows), with the firm one_ending. No arithmetic.

'A different line ending from Windows' is the negation of the same join (linux : not (uses_line_ending some (inv(uses_line_ending) value windows))), which follows from Func(uses_line_ending) and lf != crlf. No arithmetic.
